question_text: An endangered species of bird has population $217$. However, with a successful breeding program it is expected to increase by $42\%$ each year.

subparts.stem: Find the expected population size after: $5$ years

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculating value and rounding appropriately: approximately 1250 birds

subparts.solution:
$$u_5 = 217 \times (1.42)^5 \approx 1252.86$$
$$\text{The expected population size after 5 years is approximately } 1250 \text{ birds.}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Geometric growth with initial population $u_0$ and growth multiplier $r = 1 + \text{rate}$ is modeled by $u_n = u_0 r^n$.
step_by_step: Round to an appropriate degree of accuracy (e.g., 3 significant figures: 1250).
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using $n - 1$ in the exponent when $u_0$ represents the initial population.

subparts.stem: Find the expected population size after: $10$ years.

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculating value and rounding appropriately: approximately 7230 birds

subparts.solution:
$$u_{10} = 217 \times (1.42)^{10} \approx 7233.41$$
$$\text{The expected population size after 10 years is approximately } 7230 \text{ birds.}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Calculate the population at $n = 10$ using the geometric model $u_n = u_0 r^n$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Premature rounding of the intermediate powers.

subparts.stem: How long will it take for the population to reach $30\,000$?
subparts.solution:
$$\text{We need to find when } 217 \times (1.42)^n = 30\,000.$$
$$\text{Using technology, } n \approx 14.1, \text{ so it will take approximately } 14.1 \text{ years for the population to reach } 30\,000.$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Solve an exponential equation $a \cdot b^n = c$ using logarithms or a numerical equation solver on a GDC.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Forgetting to divide by 217 before applying logarithms.
